entries.proposition: One residue decides whether a C19 steroid can enter the active site of an otherwise orthologous 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, so family membership does not by itself predict a substrate.
entries.snippet: In human and primate HSD17B12, a bulky phenylalanine amino acid at this location prevents the entrance of C19-steroids into the active site of the enzyme

entries.proposition: A published negative result on substrate use by a member of this enzyme family was overturned in this paper.
entries.snippet: Two earlier studies concluded that mouse HSD17B7 did not perform this conversion

entries.proposition: The authors attribute those earlier negatives to assay conditions, so a substrate negative in this enzyme family is condition-dependent rather than settled.
entries.snippet: those studies employed reduced concentrations of substrate and shorter incubation times, which may have influenced the observed outcomes

entries.proposition: Cells carrying no transfected enzyme still convert the substrate, so an activity assay in cells or crude extract has a non-zero endogenous floor that a control must subtract.
entries.snippet: Non-transfected cells and eGFP controls produced low levels of testosterone upon addition of androstenedione, suggesting some endogenous hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase activity in HEK-293T cells
entries.anchor: Results, Replacement of Leucine With Phenylalanine at Position 234 Inhibits Testosterone Biosynthesis in Mouse HSD17B12

entries.proposition: Members of this enzyme family are multifunctional and accept several unrelated substrates, so naming one substrate does not define the enzyme's chemistry.
entries.snippet: HSD17B7 is a multifunctional enzyme that can utilize estrone, DHT and zymosterone as substrates

entries.proposition: The authors state that attributing a conversion to one family member requires first identifying the residues responsible and then mutating them, which is the dead-mutant control as their own prerequisite.
entries.snippet: would first require the identification of the specific amino acid residues responsible for the conversion of androstenedione to testosterone
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph on HSD17B7, future work

entries.proposition: The paper's own closing position is that mouse and human orthologues differ in this redundancy, so a mouse enzymology result does not transfer to the human enzyme unexamined.
entries.snippet: human orthologs have lost this plasticity
